headline: One-time gains boost profit; core banking trends improve
summary_short: Zions Bancorporation posted Q2 FY2026 net earnings of $452M (diluted EPS $3.05, +87% y/y) as a $215M gain on Visa Class B-1 shares and $37M of SBIC gains lifted results, while core EPS excluding those items rose 10% y/y to $1.74 on 4% net interest income growth and improving credit quality.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 4% y/y to $677M as NIM expanded to 3.27% from 3.17% on lower funding costs and a favorable earning-asset mix; NIM was flat q/q. Customer-related noninterest income grew 11% y/y to $182M on broad-based fee growth, led by capital markets (+29%). Noninterest expense rose 5% y/y to $551M on higher incentive compensation and professional/legal costs, partly offset by lower FDIC assessments. Credit quality improved: net charge-offs fell to 0.06% (from 0.07%) and classified loans dropped to 3.72% of loans (from 4.43%). CET1 strengthened to 11.8% from 11.0%; Zions repurchased $75M of stock and paid a $0.45/share dividend. No forward guidance was given in the release.
